body: This PR has the label `held-for-merge`. The maintainer merges it. No agent merges it.
Test build for the maintainer: commit `364e4b4f4005f79bf702c0cf1ffd82a6de4e57df`, release profile. It did not pass a review or the full gate.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 364e4b4f4005f79bf702c0cf1ffd82a6de4e57df -->
Read-only review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.**

The rule agrees with the decision of 2026-11-20. The safety core is correct: a model that is meshed at the looser tolerance always gets the existing reduced-fidelity flag, and no check passes it silently. The blockers are about text that tells the user something false, and about the gate that the body itself calls incomplete.

### Blockers

1. `crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs:117-124` (`loose_note`), and the pins at `crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs:222`, `crates/geometry/tests/step_edge_gap.rs:218`, `crates/app/tests/import_step_edge_gap.rs:49`. The note says "checks allow 0.020 mm". That is not what the checks do:
   - At a chord of 0.02 mm, the excess over `CHORD_CAP` is 0.015 mm. That is more than `DEV_TOL` (0.01 mm).
   - `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` (`crates/app/src/model_fidelity.rs:396`) returns `Err`. The program simulation judges nothing.
   - `gate_problems` (`model_fidelity.rs:362`) then refuses each program on this model at the post. An operation whose floor is over 0.015 mm is judged stricter, not looser.
   - The inch fixture (chord 0.01524 mm, excess 0.01024 mm) gets the same result.

   The note tells the user that the checks are looser. In fact the checks are stricter, or the post refuses. Change the note so that it says what occurs. For example: "This file's edges sit up to 0.018 mm off their surfaces. The file states a tolerance of 0.010 mm. The model is meshed to 0.020 mm, at reduced accuracy. Gouge checks against it are stricter, and a program on it is refused at the post. Export the file again with a tighter tolerance to clear this." Change the three pins to agree.
2. `crates/app/src/model_fidelity.rs:58`, `:294` and `:335`. Each refusal and MCP note for a reduced-fidelity model says "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget". For a model that this PR meshes at the looser tolerance, a larger budget does not change the chord, because the edge gaps set the chord. The PR makes this false advice reachable for a new class of model. Correct the text in this PR, or file a `source:agent` issue for it (a misleading message is `P3`) and name it in the PR body.
3. The gate is not complete, as the body also says.
   - The 251 app heavy steps did not run. The body says "This PR is not ready until they run".
   - The body does not list `crates/app/tests/step_fidelity.rs`. That binary pins `Milling-test.step` and `fig8.step` (each states 0.01 mm) at full fidelity through the app importer. `Milling-test.step` has no new pin in this PR, so `step_fidelity` is its only pin.
   - Run the two, and record the result in the body before the PR is flagged ready.

### Notes

- **Rule against the decision.** `EdgeGapCap::from_stated` gives `clamp(2 x stated, 0.01, 0.02)`. Zero, a negative value, NaN, infinity and `f64::MAX` are unit-tested. When two contexts disagree, the least value is used (`stated_uncertainty`). That direction is the strict one. The inch conversion is pinned by a fixture. A metre file and a file with two contexts have no fixture.
- **No file can go past 0.02 mm.** The cap is clamped. `loose_chord_mm` is `min(2 x stated, 0.02)`, and it applies only when the file states a tolerance and the measured gap is larger than the chord. After a loosen at 0.02 mm, the next refusal gets `None`, and the file is refused. The facet-budget path (#1054) can still make a chord coarser after this. That is the existing law, and it is flagged.
- **A file with no stated tolerance** keeps 0.01 mm, the old refusal start, and no loosened mesh. Pinned at 0.009 mm and 0.011 mm. `bspline_discontinuous.step` keeps its text. `import_step_guard_default_cap` is unchanged and green in the body.
- **The flag on each path.** The change is in `camcraft_geometry::step::read`. Thus `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel`, the script API, MCP import and `ImportFixture` get the chord through `Graded::coarse_mm`. The project file saves and restores it (`project/apply.rs:757`, `:792`). Stock copies, setup clones and undo carry it (#1056). There is no second derivation of the fidelity law.
- **The mesh.** The machining-mesh law is not changed. The mesh is watertight or refused, and its measured deviation plus `SNAP_MOVE_MM` must be at or under the chord (`machining_mesh.rs:317-341`). The weld snaps at 1e-9 mm and does not read edge or vertex tolerances. The raised tolerances (3 x the gap, up to 0.06 mm) go only into the kernel trim of one face. No weld merges two vertices of a small feature by them.
- **Edges that the reader fits itself** (closed-form pcurves, and the file that states 5 mm) do not go through the kernel gap check. The reader limits them with its own `MAX_TOLERANCE` (1 mm), as on `main`. The mesh deviation law is their guard. This is not a regression, but "no edge over 0.02 mm" is true only for the kernel-made trims.
- `raised_edge_gap` (`step_edge_gap.rs:147-154`) copies the margin 1.5 from a private constant of solidcore-step (`EDGE_GAP_MARGIN`). It is an upper bound. It can start a loosened mesh on a file whose tolerances were raised for a different reason, but that model is then flagged. Thus it is safe. No test pins it directly. The "up to" figure of the note can be larger than 0.02 mm.
- The new note always gives mm. The model page uses the document unit (`model_fidelity::within`).
- **Fixtures.** The seven files in `testdata/models/edge_gap/` are ours: generated, with a provenance header in `FILE_DESCRIPTION`, and legal Part 21 by a read. The commit has no copy and no excerpt of the private user file. Only measured numbers of it are in the body and the decision file.
- **Tests.** 15 new `#[test]`. No existing test or assert is changed. The tests assert chords, deviation, flags and full texts, not only "imports". The placement and the Gate maps agree with the Testing rules.
- **Laws.** No new `camcraft-*` edge, and no Cargo.toml change. Each changed file is under 400 lines (the largest is 372). There is no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests. The decision file states the `DEV_TOL` cost and what the user loses.
- **Body.** It has the `Changelog:` row and the closing line. It has no line about the test build for the maintainer that the issue promises.
- **Overlap with #2934.** This PR does not change `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs`. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads is clean.

This PR keeps `held-for-merge`. No agent merges it. The maintainer merges it.

Read-only delta review (Opus). Not built here.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This verdict is for the whole PR at this head. It replaces the earlier verdict on 364e4b4f4, and it withdraws that change request.

Scope of the review: `git diff 364e4b4f4 9185037cb` (the two review-fix commits), and `git show --remerge-diff 7b2dba40d`. The remerge-diff is empty, so the merge of `main` is class SAME. A trial merge of this head with the current `origin/main` (30f308211) is clean.

### Blockers

None.

### The three earlier blockers

1. **The note.** The kernel note now gives only the facts: the gap, the file's tolerance, and "reduced accuracy (0.020 mm)". The app adds one sentence from `loosened_consequence` (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs`). That function calls `model_fidelity::excess` and `verify::excess_floor(DEV_TOL, ..)`. `verdict_tol` uses the same two calls, so the law is not derived a second time.
   - Where `excess_floor` returns `None`, `verdict_tol` returns `Err`. Then `gate_problems` refuses each program while a non-fixture model with that chord is in the document. "A program cannot be posted while this model is in the document." is true.
   - Where it returns `Some`, the checks are tightened, and `op_problem` refuses an operation that its floor does not cover. The second sentence is true.
   - The boundary: at a chord of exactly 0.015 mm, `0.015 - 0.005` is `9.999999999999998e-3` in `f64`. The tolerance left is about 1.7e-18 mm, so the "stricter" branch applies. `verdict_tol` reads the same arithmetic, so the note and the gate agree at the boundary. Only the description of the threshold as "0.015 mm or more" is not exact. At 0.02 mm and at 0.01524 mm, the note says "cannot be posted". These are the chords that the fixtures give, and they are pinned.
   - `StepMesh.loosened` is `gap_note.is_some()`. `gap_note` is set only on the retry path. The sentence goes on the first note, and that note is the gap note. The fixtures that the tests track assert `!loosened`.
   - The text is plain English, with no jargon.
2. **The advice.** Six texts name the two remedies: `TOO_COARSE`, the MCP note in `facts`, the `op_problem` text of a kind that cannot read the excess, the vouch refusal, the model-page hint in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`, and the `import_model` tool description.
   - Each text is true for the two causes. Each changed text has a pin with the full new text, or a new assert: `model_fidelity`, `coarse_laws`, `coarse_rims`, `fidelity_copies`, `vouch_fidelity`, ui `model_fidelity`, ui `model_incomplete`.
   - No assert is weaker. The ui `model_incomplete` check changed its first expected phrase to the new hint start and added one more phrase.
   - The decision file says that the document does not record the cause, and that #2996 adds that record.
3. **The gate.** The body and the "Addressed" comment report the merged tree:
   - kernel: 119 passed;
   - geometry STEP binaries: 28 passed;
   - app: 26 binaries, 125 passed, `step_fidelity` included;
   - the `camcraft-ui` lib: 1319 passed;
   - clippy: clean for four crates;
   - a release subset of 21 heavy steps: all kernel heavy steps, and app `adaptive_fig8_crossing`, `import_solidcraft` and `large_models`.

   The body says that the other heavy steps go to the cut gate.

### Interaction with #2934

There is no interaction. #2934 adds one call in `machining_mesh::planned`: `mesh_redivide::redivide`, after `judge` and before the deviation measure. `redivide` returns notes only. It adds no `MeshRefusal` variant and renames none. `FaceCapped` and `EdgeCapped` come from `judge`, which runs before the new call. `Deviation` is still measured on the plan as it then stands. Thus the retry of this PR catches the same three refusals. The body says that the `Lobe.step` numbers did not change after the merge.

### Notes

- The heavy-subset line says "0 failed", but it also lists "the two known fails of #2845 (red as expected)". The two statements do not agree. Write them the same way in the body: for example, "0 new failures; the two known fails of #2845 are red, as on `main`".
- The body has the test-build line (the maintainer tested the build of 364e4b4f4), "Posting waits for #2996" with its `Refs` line, the `Changelog:` row and the closing line for issue 2976.
- The PR has no review label and no `held-for-merge` label. It is still a draft. The merging session flags it ready before the merge.
- The notes of the first review that are not blockers stay as they were: no metre fixture and no fixture with two contexts; `raised_edge_gap` copies a private margin of solidcore-step; the new note always gives mm.
